R061-01.notes: A (no persuasion; closing is settled), C (trumpet is a cheap student model and is not said to go to the dealer), and D (no argument) are each contradicted by the text. 'Record of trust' is an interpretive label, but a fair one given the back-page list and 'People always mean to bring things back.'

R061-02.notes: 'He only wanted to know what had been there' and 'I'll read it.' A is contradicted by 'Not to sell it.' B is wrong because the new owners take the cases and no list is required. C has no support.

R061-03.notes: 'Instead he opened the ledger...' sets up the contrast directly. B (rude), C (the trumpet was cheap) and D (the man's reason) have no support.

R061-04.notes: He 'drew a neat stroke through' a ledger line, so 'line' fits. The other choices are common meanings that do not fit the context.

R061-05.notes: Directly stated. B uses the word 'dented' as a trap.

R061-06.notes: The list is defined as things that 'had gone out the door and not come back', so A contradicts that definition. C is wrong because the trumpet was cheap. D is wrong because some entries are thirty years old. 'Most' undersells 'all but one', but it is still accurate. 'Never returned' is right in effect, since the store is closing. The passage implies the items were borrowed rather than stating it, through the trumpet example and Arno's line.

R061-07.notes: The best case for A: he kept a decades-long tally. But his calm, even tone and the quiet thanks argue against anger. Nothing supports B or D. C matches the generous reading of 'mean to.'

R061-08.notes: 'My uncle Arno' plus first-person narration. The narrator is Arno's niece or nephew.

R061-09.notes: A is a literal-minded trap: nothing suggests the narrator is clumsy. B is wrong because he keeps the ledger. C has no support. D fits the ledger's importance to him throughout.

flags.note: The phrase 'found a line I had not seen him write' (paragraph 4) suggests the narrator was watching from the ladder while Arno opened the back page. That gives choice C slight surface appeal. The narrator only 'looked at the back page' after climbing down, though, so B is still clearly the single best answer. No change needed.

R061-10.notes: 'I climbed down from the ladder and looked at the back page' comes after the man leaves. A is wrong because the ledger already held numbers. D is wrong because the list is read before the last day.

passage_consistency_notes: No blocking inconsistency. Timeline: the man borrowed the trumpet in high school in 1987 and is 'only a few years younger than Arno,' so Arno was roughly in his early twenties in 1987. He was already lending shop instruments then, which is plausible, and the ledger has been kept 'for decades.' 'Some were thirty years old' fits a present day of about 2017 or later. The five days of counting fit the fourth-afternoon visit and the last-day noon close.
